Meet the ball with a straight hitting arm. A bent elbow at contact costs both power and accuracy.
Contact the ball at the top of your reach, not out in front of your chest.
Keep the trunk close to upright. Leaning back sends the serve long.
Raise the tossing arm and hold it up. Dropping it early pulls the hitting shoulder down with it.
Keep both elbows straight and joined. Bending them makes the pass unpredictable.
Load into an athletic stance. Passing with straight legs takes away your control.
Angle the chest forward over the platform rather than standing upright.
Square, level shoulders keep the platform flat and the pass on target.
Meet the ball above and slightly in front of the forehead, not down at chin height.
Elbows bent and out on contact, so you can push through the ball.
Bend the knees before the set. The power comes from the legs, not the wrists.
Follow through until the arms are straight and the hands finish toward the target.
Bend the knees from a balanced stance before an in-place jump. Take off from the same spot.
Contact with the hitting arm straight, above the shoulder.
Drive the hips upward. Measured against your own standing hip height.
Snap the chest forward through contact instead of hanging back.
Lock both elbows at the top of the block. Bent arms collapse under a hard hit.
Close enough that the ball cannot pass between the hands, wide enough to cover the seam.
Reach the hands over and past the net line rather than straight up.
Bend the knees to load. Blocking flat-footed means late hands.
